title: Warmth slopes for within-month moth catch differences had both signs in four British samples in 1992-2015
abstract: We tested whether warm months had larger differences in caught moth taxon shares between nights. We used 383 trap-months at seven English and two Scottish sites in 1992-2003 and 2004-2015. A two-draw measure gave equal weight to retained nights and corrected a finite-catch term under independent multinomial sampling. Main warmth slopes were +0.14, +0.93, -0.40 and -0.59 percentage points per C. All four adjusted intervals included zero. A sampling-date spread control gave a positive interval only in later England. Other fitted variants gave no clear difference. High-catch filters left too few Scottish records. These results do not show a common warmth response or prove no response. Coarse weather, selected catch dates, few Scottish records and weather-dependent capture limit inference. Code, source hashes, aggregate results, checks and a figure are included. External raw data and record-level derivatives are excluded and can be regenerated in separate scratch.

display.caption: Warmth slopes for within-night and between-night two-draw diversity and their paired difference. Intervals adjust for four country-period tests within each outcome.
